topic_candidates.title: When an AI Agent Gets Permission to Touch Your Files
topic_candidates.query: NIST AI agents tool use permissions security 2025
topic_candidates.brief: An evidence-backed look at the shift from chatbots that generate text to agents that browse, edit files, call APIs and take actions. The useful angle is how permissions, tool boundaries and audit trails become the new software workflow problem.
topic_candidates.evidence_summary: Current demand: High, closely connected to the strongest AI trend seed and growing developer interest in agentic workflows. Visual potential: Excellent—show the difference between a model producing an answer and an agent executing a chain of tools. Evidence strength: High; NIST describes agents as systems that perceive environments and manipulate tools, while documenting the need for clearer capability and limitation taxonomies. Broad curiosity: High because the mechanism affects work, security and personal data. Novelty: Stronger than a generic “AI agents explained” video if centered on the permission layer and failure points. ([nist.gov](https://www.nist.gov/news-events/news/2025/08/lessons-learned-consortium-tool-use-agent-systems?utm_source=openai))

topic_candidates.title: The Power Grid Is Learning to Schedule AI Work
topic_candidates.query: Department of Energy flexible AI data center load grid 2026
topic_candidates.brief: A timely industry-shift explainer about AI data centers becoming controllable electrical loads. Instead of revisiting cooling, it examines how batch inference, workload scheduling, batteries and power contracts could help data centers respond to grid conditions.
topic_candidates.evidence_summary: Current demand: High, building on the supplied data-center concern signal while avoiding the previously used air-versus-liquid premise. Visual potential: Excellent—show an AI workload queue shifting in time, batteries smoothing peaks and a grid operator balancing demand. Evidence strength: High; U.S. Department of Energy materials describe AI loads as unusually flexible because many tasks can be batched, scheduled and orchestrated, and identify batteries as a potential flexibility resource. Broad curiosity: High because it connects invisible software scheduling to electricity bills, new power plants and local grid stress. Novelty: Very strong for a technology audience because the central mechanism is software-controlled electricity demand rather than data-center hardware. ([energy.gov](https://www.energy.gov/documents/pios202-25-11exhibits41to60?utm_source=openai))
